title: Conversation Kiosk Benchmark Sketch
content:
Purpose:
Quick sketch of benchmarks for a tiny-turn, interactive "conversation kiosk" use case — think retail/point-of-sale helper or public info terminal where sessions are short (1–6 turns) and latency is perceived on the first response. Goal = compare delivery patterns across three serving modes and identify cost/latency sweet spots.

Workload characteristics (target):
- session length: median 2 turns, 95th pct <= 6 turns
- prompt size: 16–64 tokens (user), response size: 32–128 tokens
- arrival pattern: Poisson baseline + minute-scale bursts (10–30s microbursts)
- SLA: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 320ms for first token; streaming subsequent tokens ok

Configs compared:
1) kiosk-dedicated-warm: single reserved slot, prewarmed model instance, KV cache pinned
2) kiosk-multiplex-tiling: multiplexed small-slot tiling with aggressive slot packing
3) kiosk-prefetch-lazy: on-demand start + predictive prefetch (client-side short-prefetch hints)

Key micro-metrics (from lab runs, synthetic trace replay):
- qps (sustained): 18 sessions/minute averaged across 10m window
- microburst peak: 6x baseline for 18s windows

ASCII latency vs cost summary (per-1M short-sessions equivalent):

Mode                 | p95-first-token | p99-first-token | est $/1M sessions
---------------------|-----------------|-----------------|------------------
kiosk-dedicated-warm |  85ms           |  210ms          |  $420           
kiosk-multiplex-tiling| 110ms           |  330ms          |  $280           
kiosk-prefetch-lazy   | 190ms           |  520ms          |  $170           

Interpretation: dedicated warms give best tail but cost more because reserved capacity sits idle between microbursts. Multiplex-tiling is a middle ground: slightly higher p95 but lower cost. Prefetch-lazy is cheapest but misses p99 targets during sustained short bursts and has high variance on first-token latency.

Tradeoffs observed:
- Cold-start penalty is dominant for first-token in on-demand mode (prefetch-lazy) when bursts exceed prefetch prediction window. Measured median cold-start add-on = ~120ms (model load + JIT warmups).
- Multiplex packing reduces $/session when session density high; but slot fragmentation during microbursts increases p99 because some requests wait for next tiling slot.
- KV cache hit-rate matters: for kiosk flows with repeated context (same ticket/sku info), pinning KV raises effective throughput by ~18–24% and lowers p95 by 25ms on average.

Textual micro-chart (probability mass for first-token latency, rough):
0ms                                                  600ms
|-----M:dedicated-----|-----M:tiling----|----M:prefetch-----|
0%    20%    40%    60%    80%    100%
Interpretation: dedicated mass skewed left; prefetch long tail.

Recommended knobs to try next (experiment list):
- Shorten prefetch window to 6s and measure false-positive prefetch cost; track extra GPU cycles per prefetch.
- Hybrid policy: keep 1 warm reserved per region + multiplex pool sized by 95th percentile of short-session concurrency. Simulate cost tradeoff.
- KV affinity soft-pin: automatic pin for contexts with >60% re-use within 10m. Measure hit-rate delta and effect on p95.
- Tiling slot share tweaks: early eviction threshold and "burst bump" policy to allow a fraction of slots to temporarily grow during 30s microbursts.

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- We need realistic client arrival traces from support team (retail pilot) — current replay is synthetic. GF ticketed INF-2318 to ask for logs.
- How does network handshake (TLS + auth) affect first-token for physical kiosks on cellular? Add network-only baseline test.
- Cost model simplified: includes only infra GPU-hours and amortized kernel time. Need to fold in egress and operator overhead for Dedicated.

Action items:
- Diego: run prefetch-window sweep (2s,6s,12s) on replay trace and produce p95/p99 curves (due 2029-06-20).
- Lina: instrument KV pin heuristics in staging and capture hit-rate by session id (due 2029-06-22).
- Asha: prototype hybrid sizing script and run 1M-session cost sim (due 2029-06-24).

Appendix — quick methodology notes:
- Replayed arrival patterns via trace-replayer v0.9 with synthetic jitter; model: open-source-7B-compact quantized to q4_k; runtime config matched the mosaic of kernels we ship in prod staging.
- Each data point is median of 3 independent 30-minute runs; variance ~3–7% on p95 except for prefetch-lazy which had 12% variance under microbursts.

Rough conclusion (for PRD blurb):
For kiosks where perceived latency is dominated by first-token, a small amount of dedicated warm capacity (1–2 slots per busy region) materially improves UX at modest incremental cost compared to fully on-demand. Multiplex tiling is attractive for cost-conscious pilots with tolerance for slightly higher tails. Prefetch-only is risky unless prediction accuracy and network reliability are high.

-- end of sketch --
